hints: Explain that short pulses of ultrasound are generated by applying an alternating voltage to a piezoelectric quartz transducer.
Explain why a coupling medium (gel) is placed on the skin to minimise reflection and ensure transmission into the body.
Describe how ultrasound pulses are partially reflected at boundaries between tissues of different acoustic impedance.
Explain how measuring the time delay between transmission and reception gives the depth of the boundary ($s = \frac{vt}{2}$).
Explain how the intensity or amplitude of the reflected echo reveals the nature of the boundary and tissue type.
Describe how the returning echoes are detected by the same transducer via the piezoelectric effect to construct an image.
